result_text:
I fixed the four broken default scoping conventions in `ScopingConventions.java`. The full `codeanalyzer` test suite passes (334 run, 0 failures, 3 skipped), including a new test for the fixed rules.

**Changes in `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java`:**
- **HTML generated-page rules** (pkgdown, Doxygen, `<meta name="generator">`): the path pattern was `(html|html|xhtml)`, a duplicated `html`. It is now `(html|htm|xhtml)`, so `.htm` pages are covered.
- **.NET documentation XML rule:** the path pattern `.*/[.]xml` became `.*[.]xml`, so `MyAssembly.xml` matches.
- **JavaScript `// Generated by …` rule:** the path pattern `.*/[.]js` became `.*[.]js`, so `app.js` matches.
- **Gradle JavaScript rule** (build-and-deployment): the path pattern `.*[.][-]gradle[.]js` became `.*[-]gradle[.]js`, so `build-gradle.js` matches.

**New test:** `codeanalyzer/src/test/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventionsTest.java`. It runs the real default lists against sample files. It checks that `.htm` pages, `.html` and `.xhtml` pages, `MyAssembly.xml`, `app.js` and `build-gradle.js` match. It also checks that hand-written `.htm`, `.xml` and `.js` files do not, and that `build.gradle` still matches. The test reads the private lists by reflection because `ScopingConventions` has no getter for them.

I did not commit anything.
